payload.summary: The repo is the official ROCKET code (Dempster, Petitjean and Webb). The claim maps to `code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py` with `code/rocket_functions.py`. For each dataset, the script runs `num_runs` times (default 10), with `num_kernels` kernels (default 10,000). Each run generates new random kernels, transforms train and test, fits `RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=np.logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True)` and records `classifier.score` on the test set. It saves the mean and standard deviation over runs per dataset. ECG200 is one of the bake-off datasets, and the script uses the fixed UCR `_TRAIN.txt` and `_TEST.txt` split. The older `.preprint/reproduce_experiments_bakeoff.py` is an equivalent variant with a hard-coded list of the 85 bake-off datasets, ECG200 included. The repo ships no data, no dependency files and no `bakeoff.txt` names file. I have not run anything.

entrypoints.why: Main entry point. It takes -d (txt file of dataset names), -i (input dir), -o (output dir), -n (runs, default 10) and -k (kernels, default 10000). To target ECG200, make a names file containing the single line ECG200. It writes results_ucr.csv with accuracy_mean and accuracy_standard_deviation.

Older preprint-era variant. It loops over the hard-coded 85 bake-off names, which include ECG200, and writes results_bakeoff.csv. It has no dataset-selection argument, so it would run every dataset. It uses np.int, which fails on numpy >= 1.24.
Worked example on the Coffee dataset only, with 100 kernels. It is not the ECG200 claim, and its saved outputs were removed.

dataFiles.why: Not in the repo. Download the UCR archive txt version from timeseriesclassification.com (Univariate2018_arff.zip, laid out as Univariate_arff/ECG200/...). The script expects {input_path}/{name}/{name}_TRAIN.txt and _TEST.txt, with the label in column 0 and the series in the remaining columns. ECG200 should be 100 train and 100 test series.

metricSources.description: `_results[i] = classifier.score(X_test_transform, Y_test)` gives per-run test accuracy. `_results.mean()` is stored as accuracy_mean in results_ucr.csv. Nothing is printed to stdout apart from progress messages.
Authors' published per-dataset accuracy_mean and standard deviation, with an ECG200 row. It is a reference file, not computed here.
Authors' results over resampled splits. It is not the fixed split, so it is not the target metric.

payload.runInstructions:
1. Install dependencies by hand, since the repo has no requirements file: numba, numpy, pandas and scikit-learn. Pin scikit-learn below 1.2 (for example 1.1.x), because `RidgeClassifierCV(normalize=True)` was removed in 1.2. Also pin numpy below 2.0, because `np.NINF` in rocket_functions.py was removed in numpy 2.0. The preprint script's `np.int` needs numpy below 1.24. Pick a numba version compatible with that numpy.
2. Download the UCR 2018 txt archive (Univariate2018_arff.zip from timeseriesclassification.com) and unzip it to ./Univariate_arff.
3. Run: `echo ECG200 > ecg200.txt`
4. Run: `cd code && python reproduce_experiments_ucr.py -d ../ecg200.txt -i ../Univariate_arff -o ./ -n 10 -k 10000`
5. Read accuracy_mean for ECG200 from ./results_ucr.csv. No seed is set, so results vary between runs and the 10-run mean is only approximately reproducible.
warnings: The repo has no requirements, pyproject or lockfile (dependency_discover found none). The README lists only Python, Numba, NumPy and scikit-learn, with no versions.
`normalize=True` in RidgeClassifierCV only works in scikit-learn < 1.2. `np.NINF` in rocket_functions.py needs numpy < 2.0. `.preprint` scripts use `np.int`, which needs numpy < 1.24.
No random seed is set (numba np.random is unseeded), so the 10-run mean is stochastic. Exact matches are not expected, only close agreement.
The code does not z-normalise the series. ECG200 in the UCR archive is already normalised, but this is not enforced.
The data is not in the repo and the bakeoff.txt names file referenced in the README is missing. Both must be supplied externally.
The checkout includes stored results CSVs containing ECG200 rows. I did not copy any values into this map. They are the authors' numbers, not outputs of a fresh run.
`results/results_ucr_resamples.csv` covers resampled splits and does not match the fixed-split claim.

payload.summary: Run the reviewed single-dataset adapter rocket-ecg200-runner. It loads the pinned repo's code/rocket_functions.py (authors' random-kernel transform). On the fixed ECG200 train/test split it does 10 runs, each with 10,000 freshly generated kernels and RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True), as in the official script. It writes the mean of the 10 per-run test accuracies, as a fraction, to artifacts/result.json under metrics.accuracyMean. The adapter is needed because the official script fails on a one-row dataset-name file, and it also imports pandas, which is not in the allowed requirements. Wheels for all pinned requirements exist on linux/arm64 for Python 3.11. No seed is set upstream, so the run-to-run mean is stochastic.

risks: The adapter is project-owned, not official repository code. It reproduces the official loop for one dataset and does not change the algorithm.

The extracted dataset location is not confirmed. The ../data/ paths for ECG200_TRAIN.txt and ECG200_TEST.txt assume the lab extracts the archive files there. If the files land elsewhere, the paths must be adjusted.
The artifact path ../artifacts/result.json is assumed to resolve to the artifacts/result.json the metric parser reads.
No seed is set upstream (numba np.random is unseeded), so the 10-run mean varies between executions.
The series are not normalised by the code. The file is used as shipped.
Numba JIT compilation on 2 ARM CPUs adds start-up time.
